answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making identity a staked, endorsed position instead of a free address. Each new agent locks a bond and needs two endorsements from already-staked peers, who share the slashing risk if it double-signs. Growing a fake orchard is then costly: every new tree in the grove demands another full bond, and each vine of trust must be sponsored by someone with their own deposit at risk. To sway a vote, an attacker must lock a large share of the total stake, and any detected fraud burns it permanently.
